text.p: Bernie Williams hit a three-run homer and a grand slam, driving in eight runs, and David Cone struck out eight over seven innings as the New York Yankees beat the Detroit Tigers 12-3 Thursday.
The Yankees victory and Baltimore's loss to the White Sox gave New York a 3-1/2-game lead in the American League East.

Williams, who hit homers from both sides of the plate, pounded a three-run shot, his 25th, with one out in the third off starter Justin Thompson (1-5) to give the Yankees a 3-2 lead. He snapped a 3-3 tie with an RBI single in the top of the fifth and added his fourth career grand slam with two out in the ninth off Jose Lima.

"When you get eight RBI, the opportunities have to present themselves, but you still have to do it," said Yankees manager Joe Torre about Williams. "He had some great at-bats left-handed. We haven't seen that power for a while. I hope it's a sign of things to come."
In Baltimore, Alex Fernandez pitched a three-hitter and Pat Borders hit a three-run homer as the Chicago White Sox defeated the Baltimore Orioles 11-3.
Fernandez allowed three earned runs in his fifth complete game, walked two and struck out 10. The White Sox moved within one-half game of the Orioles for the American League wild-card spot.
Baltimore starter Mike Mussina (19-10) was tagged for six runs and eight hits over 3-2/3 innings, including Borders homer.

In Kansas City, Mark Whiten belted a three-run homer to key a four-run sixth inning and added a RBI single in the ninth as the Seattle Mariners kept their playoff hopes alive with an 8-5 win over the Kansas City Royals.
Terry Mulholland (4-2) allowed four runs -- three earned -- and six hits in five innings.
Seattle is 4 1/2 games behind Baltimore for the American League wild-card spot.

At Minnesota, Pat Meares' sacrifice fly with one out in the bottom of the 12th inning scored Roberto Kelly with the winning run as the Minnesota Twins edged the Oakland Athletics 4-3, keeping their slim playoff hopes alive.
Dave Stevens (3-3) held the Athletics to one hit and a walk over the final 2-2/3 innings to post the win, Minnesota's seventh in 10 games.

At Texas, Fernando Vina went 5-for-6 with two homers and three RBI and Jeromy Burnitz drove in four runs as the Milwaukee Brewers built a 10-run lead by the second inning and cruised to a 15-4 rout of the Texas Rangers.
Vina singled and scored in a six-run first inning, tripled and scored in the third, singled in the fifth, homered in the seventh and added a two-run blast in the ninth.
Ben McDonald (11-10) snapped a personal seven-game losing streak with eight solid innings.
In Cleveland, Jim Thome hit a pair of two-run homers and Julio Franco added two solo shots as the Cleveland Indians completed a four-game sweep of the California Angels with an 11-2 rout.

Cleveland jumped on Angels starter Shawn Boskie (12-10) right away as Kenny Lofton led off the first inning with a single and stole second. After Kevin Seitzer walked, Lofton stole third and came home on a wild pitch. Thome followed with his 34th homer to make it 3-0.
